Factor ordering with ysx_factors

Source: vignettes/factor-ordering.Rmd
factor-ordering.Rmd

ysx_factors() extends yspec::ys_factors() with per-variable ordering through dots$order. It converts coded values to labelled factors while retaining the original values in columns ending in _v by default.

Specify the order in YAML

Set order to first to keep the level order defined in the specification, or biggest to sort levels by decreasing frequency in the data being converted. Omitting order is equivalent to first. No other values are accepted.

SETUP__:
  description: Example factor ordering
RESPONSE:
  values: {Low: 1, Medium: 2, High: 3, Unused: 4}
  dots: {order: first}

The following example creates and loads this specification. In a project, pass the path to your existing YAML file to yspec::ys_load() instead.

library(yspecx)

spec_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
yaml::write_yaml(
  list(
    SETUP__ = list(description = "Example factor ordering"),
    RESPONSE = list(
      values = list(Low = 1, Medium = 2, High = 3, Unused = 4),
      dots = list(order = "first")
    )
  ),
  spec_path
)
spec <- yspec::ys_load(spec_path)
unlink(spec_path)

data <- data.frame(ID = seq_len(7), RESPONSE = c(3, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, NA))

Preserve specification order

first refers to specification order, not the order of first appearance in the data. Here High appears first in the data, but Low is the first factor level.

first <- ysx_factors(data, spec)
levels(first$RESPONSE)
#> [1] "Low"    "Medium" "High"   "Unused"
head(first)
#>   ID RESPONSE RESPONSE_v
#> 1  1     High          3
#> 2  2   Medium          2
#> 3  3   Medium          2
#> 4  4     High          3
#> 5  5   Medium          2
#> 6  6      Low          1

Order from biggest to smallest

Change the setting in the YAML file, or update the loaded specification:

spec$RESPONSE$dots$order <- "biggest"
biggest <- ysx_factors(data, spec)
levels(biggest$RESPONSE)
#> [1] "Medium" "High"   "Low"    "Unused"
table(biggest$RESPONSE, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#> Medium   High    Low Unused   <NA> 
#>      3      2      1      0      1

Medium occurs three times, High twice and Low once. The unused level remains last. Missing observations do not contribute to these counts unless they are an explicit factor level. The underlying observations are not sorted or changed; only the level order changes.

Frequencies are calculated from the data supplied to each call. If levels have equal counts, their relative order follows the original yspec factor order.

tied <- ysx_factors(data.frame(RESPONSE = c(3, 2)), spec)
levels(tied$RESPONSE)
#> [1] "Medium" "High"   "Low"    "Unused"

Although High appears first, Medium precedes it because they have equal counts and Medium comes first in the specification. Unused levels also keep their relative specification order.

Select columns and retain original values

Column selection and value-column options follow yspec::ys_factors(). Pass unquoted column names to restrict conversion. Use .keep_values = FALSE to omit the original codes, or .suffix to choose their column suffix.

selected <- ysx_factors(data, spec, RESPONSE, .keep_values = FALSE)
names(selected)
#> [1] "ID"       "RESPONSE"

with_codes <- ysx_factors(data, spec, RESPONSE, .suffix = "_code")
head(with_codes)
#>   ID RESPONSE RESPONSE_code
#> 1  1     High             3
#> 2  2   Medium             2
#> 3  3   Medium             2
#> 4  4     High             3
#> 5  5   Medium             2
#> 6  6      Low             1

Existing factors and validation

Existing factor columns are left unchanged, including their level order. To change the ordering after a previous conversion, call ysx_factors() on the original coded data rather than the factor output.

unchanged <- ysx_factors(first, spec)
identical(levels(unchanged$RESPONSE), levels(first$RESPONSE))
#> [1] TRUE

An invalid dots$order setting raises an error when that variable is converted. Settings on unselected variables or existing factors are not validated.
